_comment: State the recorded conversation must leave behind. Asserted as a subset:
every field here must be present with this value, and the database may know
more. Only fields the recorded tool results revealed, or state that follows
necessarily from them, are asserted.
_key_columns declares how each table is addressed, so a row is identified by
a stable business key rather than by position in the snapshot.
The headphones case is asserted unchanged. This conversation reads it twice
and the agent says explicitly that nothing about it should move, so leaving
it alone is part of what a correct handling does.
This document is read by both layers and everything in it has to be an
outcome rather than a route, so nothing a read advances is asserted here.
section_read_log is left out although the recording drives the eligibility
panel to two reads: reads_served counts how many times the agent looked,
which is the one thing the grading layer must not score.
The confirmation's status is asserted, but as a set rather than as one
value, and on this order the point is unmissable. create_replacement_order
queues the message; the recorded 'sent' is not a later event but the effect
of the one get_order that reads it, because _advance_notification collects
the next delivery receipt each time the message is looked at. Asserting
'sent' alone would be asserting that the agent read its own email exactly
once. The replacement_confirmation template hands the message over as
'queued' and its delivery progression runs through 'sent' to 'delivered', so
those three are the whole of what a correct run can leave behind and any of
them is accepted. The set still asserts something real: the message exists on
a live delivery progression and has not failed, which is what the caller was
promised, while saying nothing about how many times anybody looked at it.
status_index is not asserted. It is a bare read counter with no outcome
meaning, and it is one of the two columns the damage policy drops from the
row hash for exactly that reason.
The conformance layer pins both far harder than an assertion could: each
read depth returns a different payload and the replay is byte-exact, so a
cursor or a delivery state that advanced wrongly fails env_check.sh on the
wire.
